title: I Built 101 Indian Monuments in the Browser Using Only Code (No 3D Models)
why_read: A creative procedural-geometry project that recreates 101 Indian monuments in the browser using only code-generated 3D shapes, no model files.
analysis: The project builds each monument as a small JavaScript function composing primitive shapes like boxes, cylinders, and domes, with a single shared shader handling materials like stone, marble, and water. This is a nice demonstration of procedural generation techniques and efficient web-based 3D rendering, achieved with zero external dependencies and tiny code footprints per monument. It is more of a creative coding showcase than a deep technical innovation, but the constraints, around 2KB of code per building and no downloaded assets, are impressive from an engineering economy standpoint. Readers interested in procedural graphics or WebGL/Three.js-style techniques would likely find this inspiring and technically instructive.
